name: Gießerei Brandlhuber GmbH & Co. KG
summary: Brandlhuber is a family-owned foundry founded in 1921, with 185 staff and about EUR 25.8 M turnover. The owner negotiates personally and keeps reminding us that in 2022 they held the old price for a quarter, and he now expects 'partnership' in return. After years of settling below cost on part:310010, he has asked for +9.5 % from 2026-11-01. He admits he has not tracked his material and energy costs since 2022 and uses a two-year-old spreadsheet. He also wants faster payment.

situation.decision_maker: owner decides personally; his office manager prepares the costing

negotiation_pattern: Small asks of about +0.4 % on average, settled about 2.8 pts lower (average -2.4 %), every time below the ask. On part:310010 he repeatedly 'accepted below full cost to keep the volume'. He gives in for volume and relationship rather than fighting. The 9.5 % letter is a break from that pattern, after months of complaining that the partnership is not reciprocated. He reacts to fairness and to having his past loyalty recognised, not to hard pressure.
wants: recognition and fair treatment (the 2022 favour returned)
a price on part:310010 that at least covers his cost
faster payment: 10 days with skonto, and an end to our late payment
volume security and continuation of the framework
clarity on cost and index figures (his own data is outdated)
protects: unit_price on part:310010 (he sells it below his own cost and will not go lower)
his sense of being treated as a partner (will dig in if pressured or lectured)

trades.give: payment_days: pay within 10 days (and actually on time)
trades.get: skonto plus a clearly smaller increase on part:310010
trades.why: He asked for this himself; we pay late 84 % of the time and take no skonto, so this is a cheap give that he values highly.

trades.give: unit_price on part:310010: a moderate increase toward his should-cost (EUR 132.64), not 9.5 % (EUR 138.55)
trades.get: effective_date 2027-01-01 instead of 2026-11-01, plus a price cut on part:310012 toward EUR 370.21 or below
trades.why: Part:310010 is 4.6 % below his cost, but part:310012 is 10.3 % above his own cost. Balancing across both parts is fair and keeps our total spend flat.

trades.give: contract_months: 24-month renewal, and a higher volume_per_year / quota on part:310012 (now 40 %)
trades.get: the price reduction on part:310012 and a price hold through 2027
trades.why: Long-term commitment and steady volume are what a loyal family supplier values most.

trades.give: index_clause based on transparent public energy and material indices (we share our sources)
trades.get: a lower base price now, instead of a lump-sum markup
trades.why: He asked where our index figures come from and admits his own are two years old. A shared index answers his fairness concern without overpaying.

trades.get: ppm_commitment below 500, a plan to reach the 95 % OTD target, and the overdue 8D closed
trades.why: The scorecard turned amber and ppm is rising; tying volume to a quality plan is a fair partnership deal.

arguments.point: Prices are fixed for calendar year 2026. A change on 2026-11-01 is not possible under the contract. His notice is on time only for 2027-01-01.
We acknowledge the 2022 gesture and that part:310010 is priced tight for him. We want to fix it fairly, across both parts.
Energy and material costs have moved since the 2022 peak. Offer to go through the cost build-up together with his office manager, using our index sources.
Part:310012 is priced well above cost: +10.3 % over his own plant's estimate and +3.5 % over the other source's plant.
Partnership works both ways: OTD is 85.2 % against a 95 % target, ppm rose from 522 to 712, the scorecard is now amber, and one 8D is overdue.

avoid: Threatening to move part:310010 or the tooling to the other source. He will dig in or terminate.
Dismissing the 2022 favour or his repeated 'partnership' message.
Exploiting his outdated cost knowledge in a way he will later see as a trick (a fairness breach).
Demanding a price cut on part:310010, which is already below his cost.
Promising fast payment and then paying late again.
tone: Personal, respectful and owner-to-partner: acknowledge 2022, be transparent with numbers, propose a fair package, never ultimatums.
red_flags: Walk-away risk: the framework auto-extends unless terminated with 90 days' notice before 2026-12-31 (around 2026-10-02). He could still give notice, and part:310010 is 100 % with him.
Part:310010 sells below his own cost, so a persistent loss could make him drop or neglect the part.
Liquidity hint: the 10-day payment and skonto request. Credit index 222 is stable and equity is 24.7 %, so this is not acute but worth watching.
Quality is slipping: amber scorecard, ppm 712, 2 open 8D (1 overdue), OTD chronically about 85 %.
The recent quotes leave out validity and incoterm, so pin both down in writing.

evidence.claim: Family-owned since 1921; the owner visits personally and expects partnership for keeping old prices in 2022.
Prices are fixed per calendar year; changes need 90 days' notice before year end.
Part:310010 price is 4.6 % below his own should-cost and was repeatedly accepted below cost to keep volume.
Part:310012 price is 10.3 % above his own should-cost and 3.5 % above the other source's plant.
The owner works from a two-year-old spreadsheet and has not tracked costs since 2022; his office manager does the costing.
He asked for payment within 10 days in exchange for skonto.
Scorecard moved to amber in 2026Q3: OTD 85.2 %, ppm 712, 1 overdue 8D.
Framework expires 2026-12-31 and auto-extends 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice.

indicators.credit_index: 222 (12 months ago 222; higher is worse, >300 weak)
price_vs_should_cost_no_margin: part:310010: price 126.53 vs cost:310010 132.64 (its own plant): -4.6 %
indicators.scorecard_trend: 2025Q4 green (otd 84.9, ppm 625) → 2026Q1 green (otd 81.5, ppm 522) → 2026Q2 green (otd 83.3, ppm 626) → 2026Q3 amber (otd 85.2, ppm 712)
